trust_decision.summary: The user's full-text retrieval query is trusted as SQL text: MyScaleVector.search_by_full_text splices it inside a single-quoted ClickHouse literal and _search runs the string unbound; the only upstream escaping handles double quotes only.

landing_point.why: The summary names MyScale search_by_full_text; it is the only method of that name in the MyScale provider and holds the f-string literal.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /console/api/datasets/<id>/hit-testing (api/controllers/console/datasets/hit_testing.py:28), service API /v1/datasets/<id>/hit-testing|retrieve (api/controllers/service_api/dataset/hit_testing.py:14), inner API /knowledge/retrieve (api/controllers/inner_api/knowledge/retrieval.py:49), app/workflow knowledge retrieval via RetrievalService.retrieve (api/core/rag/datasource/retrieval_service.py:850-853)
same as above (private _search gains a parameters argument passed to client.query)
fix_sites.module_kind: vector-store provider plugin package (DB adapter, query executor)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Remaining unbound interpolations in the same file (document_ids_filter, text_exists id, metadata key/value) carry server-generated UUIDs/fixed keys, so a solver can argue they are not user-controlled.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Full-text queries containing apostrophes/backslashes (e.g. "O'Reilly") must still be searched verbatim; stripping or blanking quotes (as escape_str does for inserts) or editing the shared escape_query_for_search, which every vector store uses, changes legitimate results.

O6_input_shapes: plain str query with single quote / SQL suffix, bound as ClickHouse {query:String} server-side parameter (fix.diff:224-228, fix.diff:243)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: document_ids_filter values quoted with f"'{id}'" in the same _search WHERE clause the fix left unbound
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Filter list today comes from DB-side metadata filtering (api/core/rag/retrieval/dataset_retrieval.py:672-676); a maintainer adding a caller-supplied document filter on the retrieve API would reach it unchanged.
Same string-built SQL style; a metadata-based lookup exposed to user-defined metadata values would be a plausible addition.
doc_id can come from document metadata on import (myscale_vector.py:83); a path letting callers set doc_id would reach it.

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89), ClickHouse/MyScale string literal in vector-store full-text search

services: MyScale/ClickHouse only for integration tests; unit tests stub clickhouse_connect

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape or strip single quotes in the query (reuse escape_str or extend escape_query_for_search) instead of binding it as a ClickHouse parameter.

out_of_scope_notes: Two of the three fix commits are unrelated: 5c6372d2 is a version bump and b5e35fc2 edits docker/volumes/sandbox/conf/config.yaml; only d9884efa changes source.

Other SQL-backed providers (pgvector, opengauss, vastbase, analyticdb_sql) put f"'{query}'" into bound parameter tuples, not SQL text (e.g. api/providers/vdb/vdb-pgvector/src/dify_vdb_pgvector/pgvector.py:229-230); not pursued.
Identifier interpolation of database/collection names in MyScale DDL comes from config and dataset ids; not pursued.
unverified: j_multi_site=1 only because O1>=2 (several entry points into one sink); there is one fix site.
Whether any caller can supply document_ids_filter or metadata values directly was checked only for dataset_retrieval.py:672-676 and the annotation tasks; other callers not traced.
